task.description:
Closing gate on WF03-ISS0210-20260821. DOC-UPDATER wrote a force-with-lease rule (with boundary) into `GIT_MERGE.md` step 6, added a pointer sentence to `ORCHESTRATOR.md` section 7.1, and made an explicit per-file adopt/decline call on a `.gitattributes` union merge driver -- adopted for `handoffs/orchestrator.log`, declined for `handoffs/registry.json`. Its report is `result` in `handoffs/WF03-ISS0210-20260821/step-03-git-merge-push-gap.json`; read it there and re-derive, don't read back. Single commit `4fd5126` (docs, `.gitattributes`, this run's own handoff), local and unpushed.

You are the only gate on this run: no SECURITY-REVIEWER step, no test step, no human backstop. A PASS releases the queue task.

SCOPE OF `result.issues` ON THIS DISPATCH: report a MINOR only for a defect -- something that fails a criterion, contradicts another document, states a false checkable claim, or would mislead a later agent. Not style or wording preference.

RE-DERIVE. Each item names what you must run or open yourself:

1. THE CORE CLAIM IS OPERATIONAL, NOT JUST TEXTUAL -- CHECK WHETHER THE NEW RULE ACTUALLY WORKS. Read the new step 6 text in `GIT_MERGE.md`. Confirm it states: (a) an ordinary push is tried first and suffices when the rebase was a no-op, (b) on rejection, `--force-with-lease` (never bare `--force`) republishes ONLY the run's own `feature/<run-id>` branch, (c) the authorization never extends to `main` or to a commit authored by another session. Then stress-test it against the scenario that motivated this issue: pretend you are `WF03-ISS0200-20260821`'s Step Final again -- would following the NEW text produce the same safe outcome that agent reached by improvisation (or a safe outcome by a different correct path), without needing ORCH to intervene mid-step this time? If the new text would still leave an agent stuck or would license something dangerous (e.g. force-with-lease is phrased loosely enough to read as covering `main`), that is a FAIL.

2. VERIFY THE NON-FAST-FORWARD RE-DERIVATION FROM THE ACTUAL SOURCE. Open `handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json` yourself and confirm it really does show what the step-03 report says it shows -- a rebase that replayed commits followed by a push conflict, not a inference.

3. AUTOCRLF -- RE-RUN THE CHECK YOURSELF. `git config --get core.autocrlf` on this host, plus your own before/after comparison of a file's working-tree bytes vs its git blob (`git show HEAD:<path> | sha256sum` vs the checked-out file's hash) for at least one file. Confirm the step's reported hashes and CRLF/LF finding, or say if you get something different. Confirm any byte-identity guidance added names the blob, not the working tree.

4. THE UNION-DRIVER DECISION -- JUDGE THE REASONING, NOT JUST THE OUTCOME. Read `.gitattributes`. For `orchestrator.log`: is a `merge=union` driver actually a safe fit for this specific file (flat, append-only, one line per event, no ordering dependency the union driver could scramble)? For `registry.json`: is the declined-adoption reasoning about JSON structural risk correct and sufficiently explained, or does it read as a hedge? Either verdict is acceptable if the reasoning holds -- judge the reasoning.

5. CONSISTENCY, NOT DUPLICATION. Read `ORCHESTRATOR.md` section 7.1's new sentence in context. Confirm it clarifies rather than restates, and that the rule lives in exactly one place (`GIT_MERGE.md` step 6).

6. ISSUE CLOSURE. `docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml` carries `status: resolved`, `resolved_in_run`, a plausible clock-read `resolved_at`. Confirm GH#402 is actually closed with `gh issue view 402 --json state,closedAt` -- do not take the report's word for it.

7. BOOKKEEPING AND SCOPE. `git show --stat 4fd5126`: only `.gitattributes`, `docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md`, `docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md`, `docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml` and this run's own handoff may appear -- no `lib/`, `priv/`, `test/`, `web/`, and no historical handoff backfilled. `HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` section 1.2 and its `git_evidence` subsection must be untouched by this commit (check whether ISS-0206/ISS-0208 are still open against section 1.2 via a queue check or by their absence of a `resolved` status in their yaml, and confirm this run did not quietly resolve either). Step 03's `result.status` is `PASS` (legal). `handoffs/orchestrator.log` and `handoffs/registry.json` are ORCH's, deliberately uncommitted -- confirm `git diff --numstat` shows 0 deletions on both and leave them alone.

VERDICT: PASS or FAIL against the seven acceptance criteria on the Step 03 handoff plus the items above. A FAIL names each failed criterion and the specific gap. Commit your own handoff file. Do not write `registry.json` or `orchestrator.log`, and do not edit `docs/` unless correcting to avoid a FAIL, stated explicitly; you are a gate, not a producer.

result.summary:
REVIEWER gate on WF03-ISS0210-20260821 Step 03. FAIL -- one genuine defect found on re-derivation (check 2 / AC2), everything else re-derived clean. Routed back for a wording-only correction, not a rework of the substantive rule.

1) STRESS TEST (AC1) -- the RULE itself PASSES. GIT_MERGE.md step 6 now states: try a plain push first (a no-op rebase needs no force); on an actual rejection, --force-with-lease -- never bare --force -- republishes ONLY the run's own feature/<run-id> branch; the authorization never extends to main or another session's commit, and ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1's prohibition on those is stated unchanged. Replaying WF03-ISS0200-20260821's Step Final against this text: since GIT_MERGE.md is read directly by ELIXIR-DEV/FRONTEND-DEV (not only by ORCH), the executing agent now has an authoritative, correctly-scoped rule in the protocol itself and would not need to wait for ORCH to write (and then mid-step correct) an over-broad 'do NOT force-push under any circumstance' instruction. Either resolution path the original run could have taken -- force-with-lease on its own branch, or the reset+merge it actually used -- is already licensed or left open by the new text. The rule closes the structural gap.

2) NON-FAST-FORWARD CLAIM RE-DERIVED FROM SOURCE (AC2) -- FAILS. Opened handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-final-git-merge.json directly, not the step-03 report's summary of it. The source does NOT show 'a rebase that replayed commits followed by a push conflict.' It shows the opposite of a conflict: the run's own narrative states the branch was rebased once (pushed fast-forward, since the branch had been pushed empty at Step 00), then origin/main moved a second time; rather than rebase again on top of already-published commits and risk the rejection, the run explicitly RESET back to its published tip and MERGED origin/main into it instead -- 'It was resolved WITHOUT force ... the branch was reset back to its published tip and origin/main was MERGED into it instead' -- then proved tree equivalence to the discarded rebase. git_evidence.push_status confirms: 'pushed, fast-forward only ... no force-push and no --force-with-lease issued at any point.' No push was ever rejected in that run. That run's own result.issues[0] says so accurately: 'It did not block this step ... but AS WRITTEN it WOULD deadlock' -- hypothetical, not experienced. ISS-0210.yaml's own original description (line 26) is equally accurate: 'The agent did NOT use the authorization -- it reset to the published tip and merged origin/main instead.'

Against that, two places in THIS commit misstate the same source as empirical proof of an actual rejection: GIT_MERGE.md step 6 says '(Confirmed live, not just from the protocol text: WF03-ISS0200-20260821's Step Final hit exactly this after its branch was rebased twice -- see that run's step-final-git-merge.json, result.issues[0].)', and ISS-0210.yaml's own resolved_at/resolution_note says '...WF03-ISS0200-20260821's step-final-git-merge.json result.issues[0], which hit a live rejection this way.' Both are false checkable claims, and both directly contradict ISS-0210.yaml's own unedited description field two paragraphs above the resolution_note in the SAME file. The underlying structural argument (rebase rewrites the branch, remote holds the pre-rebase tip, therefore a plain push would be rejected) is sound and needs no empirical proof -- it follows from git mechanics -- but claiming it was 'confirmed live' by a citation that shows the opposite will mislead a future reader who checks the citation less carefully than this gate did, into treating an avoided scenario as a tested one.

3) AUTOCRLF -- RE-RUN FIRST-HAND (AC3), CONFIRMED. `git config --get core.autocrlf` -> true, this host. Blob vs. working-tree hash for docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md: `git show HEAD:...` sha256 8075a0552c251aa81348159ff10ac1da7c4d25314c52b4a22c6ca513de9cdb58, working-tree file sha256 2cc9a892ee010b2a0f2497e33af743641168b0395a11cac817c2aace7e03b02 -- different, confirming the CRLF rewrite is live and the reported finding reproduces. GIT_MERGE.md's new guidance (step 5b area) names the git blob (`git show <sha>:<path>` / `git cat-file blob <sha>`) as the required hashing target, never the working-tree file -- confirmed.

4) UNION-DRIVER REASONING JUDGED PER FILE (AC4), SOUND for both. orchestrator.log: flat, append-only, one line per event, no ordering dependency a line union could scramble -- merge=union is a genuine fit, and the .gitattributes comment cites the actual prior run's evidence (line count only grew, origin/main's lines an exact prefix) rather than asserting it. registry.json: JSON structure means two concurrent appends commonly touch the SAME closing brace/bracket lines; a naive line union can produce invalid or duplicate-keyed JSON -- this is a real structural risk, correctly explained with the specific failure mechanism (not a hedge), and hand-resolution is correctly left mandatory. Neither verdict is asserted without its mechanism.

5) ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1 (AC5), CONFIRMED. The addition is exactly one sentence pointing at GIT_MERGE.md step 6 ('a different rule from a run republishing its OWN rebased feature branch, which is authorized, scoped, and stated in full at GIT_MERGE.md step 6 ... read it there rather than inferring either rule from the other'), not a restatement of the force-with-lease rule's content. The rule lives in exactly one place.

6) ISSUE CLOSURE (AC6), CONFIRMED independently. `gh issue view 402 --json state,closedAt` -> {"closedAt":"2026-08-21T11:23:28Z","state":"CLOSED"}. docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml carries status: resolved, resolved_in_run: WF03-ISS0210-20260821, resolved_at: 2026-08-21T11:23:04Z (read from the file, not the report).

7) BOOKKEEPING AND SCOPE (AC7), CONFIRMED. `git show --stat 4fd5126` touches exactly five paths: .gitattributes, docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md, docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md, docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml, and this run's own step-03 handoff -- no lib/, priv/, test/, web/, and no historical handoff backfilled. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.2 does not appear in the commit; docs/issues/ISS-0206.yaml and ISS-0208.yaml both still read `status: open` and neither was touched by this commit. Step 03's result.status is PASS (legal, matches the acceptance list). `git diff --numstat -- handoffs/orchestrator.log handoffs/registry.json` shows 8/0 and 20/0 (insertions/deletions) -- 0 deletions on both, neither committed by 4fd5126, left alone as required.

VERDICT: FAIL on AC2 only. All other criteria (AC1, AC3-AC9) hold. This is a wording-only defect -- two sentences overclaiming empirical confirmation of a scenario the cited source shows was avoided, not experienced -- not a defect in the rule itself, which is correct, safely scoped, and would close the real gap the next time a Step Final's push is actually rejected.

issues.description: GIT_MERGE.md step 6's parenthetical '(Confirmed live, not just from the protocol text: WF03-ISS0200-20260821's Step Final hit exactly this after its branch was rebased twice -- see that run's step-final-git-merge.json, result.issues[0].)' is a false checkable claim. That handoff's own narrative and git_evidence.push_status show every push in that run was a plain fast-forward and no push was ever rejected -- the run avoided the rejection by resetting to its published tip and merging origin/main in rather than rebasing again, then proving tree equivalence. That run's own result.issues[0] says accurately 'as written it WOULD deadlock' (hypothetical), and ISS-0210.yaml's own unedited description field says accurately 'The agent did NOT use the authorization.' Fix: reword to state the run's dispatch was corrected mid-step because the (real, structural) deadlock risk was anticipated, and that the agent in fact avoided ever needing the push by choosing reset+merge over a second rebase -- do not claim the rejection itself was observed.

docs/issues/ISS-0210.yaml's resolution_note repeats the same overclaim: '...WF03-ISS0200-20260821's step-final-git-merge.json result.issues[0], which hit a live rejection this way.' This directly contradicts the same file's own unedited description field two paragraphs above it, which correctly states the agent avoided using the authorization by resetting to the published tip and merging. Fix alongside the GIT_MERGE.md wording.

git_evidence.push_status: skipped -- docs-only gate, no feature branch under this run

result.next_action: ORCH routes back to DOC-UPDATER for a rework: reword the two overclaiming sentences (GIT_MERGE.md step 6's parenthetical and ISS-0210.yaml's resolution_note) to accurately describe WF03-ISS0200-20260821's Step Final as an anticipated-but-avoided deadlock, not an observed rejection. No other content changes needed; do not touch the force-with-lease rule itself, the .gitattributes decision, or the pointer sentence in ORCHESTRATOR.md 7.1, all of which passed. Re-dispatch to REVIEWER for a narrow re-gate once reworded.
